root_cause.text: The Mediatek clock driver marked `struct mtk_gate` arrays as `__initconst`, but after refactoring in commit 8ceff24a754a those gate descriptors are referenced at runtime by the clk-gate code, so they could be discarded into freed init-only memory and later accessed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “the mtk_gate structs are no longer just used for initialization/registration, but also at runtime. So drop __initconst annotations,” and the patch removes `__initconst` from `sgmii0_clks`, `sgmii1_clks`, `eth_clks`, and `top_clks` in the Mediatek clock driver.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable pattern: multiple clock descriptor arrays are declared with init-only lifetime, e.g. `static const struct mtk_gate top_clks[] __initconst = { ... };` and `static const struct mtk_fixed_clk fixed_clks[] __initconst = { ... };` as well as many parent-name arrays using `__initconst`. These descriptors are then passed to runtime registration code, e.g. `mtk_clk_register_gates(node, top_clks, ARRAY_SIZE(top_clks), clk_data);` and `mtk_clk_register_composites(...);`. Because the Mediatek clk-gate code references gate descriptors at runtime, marking `top_clks` as `__initconst` is the vulnerable construct. There is no fix present in this function body: the arrays are still marked `__initconst`, and there is no conversion to non-init storage or other lifetime-safe handling.
